daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Demokrat leaders have moved to contain speculation about party chairman AHY's presidential ambitions for 2029, following recent speeches that touched on themes of power and governance. The party denied AHY's recent speech on power was connected to the 2029 presidential race, directly rebutting assessments from Gerindra and Golkar that the chairman is already preparing a candidacy. However, Golkar interpreted AHY's gestures as signalling readiness to run, while Gerindra noted the election remains far off.

  • Investor and capital market figure Andry Hakim has officially joined the Demokrat party, adding a prominent business personality to its ranks.
  • Coordinating Minister for the Economy Airlangga announced that 30-kg rice assistance will continue until December in response to El Niño conditions.
  • The DPR has drafted a land reform bill that limits land holdings and establishes a special implementing body.
  • DPR member Sahroni guaranteed the asset forfeiture bill will be enacted by 15 December, though he noted it may not satisfy all parties.
  • A DPR member has assured the asset forfeiture bill will not allow authorities to act arbitrarily, while a legal expert stated asset seizure authority must be held by a trusted institution.
  • The KPK suspects the wife of Pemalang regent prepared funds obtained through extortion.
  • Minister of State Apparatus Empowerment is pushing transformation in public services from one-stop service centres to integrity zones.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia joined Arab and Islamic nations in issuing a joint condemnation of Israeli calls to expel Palestinians from Gaza. The Foreign Ministry condemned statements by Zionist officials supporting the forced removal of Gazans, with eight countries jointly denouncing the Israeli position. President Prabowo separately discussed defence procurement, mentioning Black Hawk helicopters during talks on the Garibaldi aircraft carrier acquisition.

  • Indonesia and Malaysia strengthened police cooperation to combat cross-border drug trafficking.
  • Indonesia is seeking stronger religious tourism ties with Uzbekistan to expand bilateral cooperation in the sector.
  • The government's communications office explained Prabowo's upcoming visit to Russia is aimed at opening economic opportunities for Indonesia.
  • MPR Deputy Speaker Fadli Zon was featured discussing cultural diplomacy approaches in a special programme.

Other

The Anak Krakatau eruption has caused massive disruption to air travel and economic activity, with authorities reporting significant impacts across multiple sectors. The eruption affected 341,000 flight passengers, with 2,961 flights disrupted at airports across Java and Sumatra. Economists warn that forest fires and volcanic ash threaten up to Rp 123.1 trillion in economic activity, though continuous eruption has ended according to the Geological Agency.

  • Soekarno-Hatta and Husein Sastranegara airports have reopened while Radin Inten remains closed, and authorities have confirmed normal operations at Soekarno-Hatta, Halim, and Husein Sastranegara.
  • The Health Ministry addressed sudden mask price increases caused by volcanic ash demand, while Banten placed all health facilities on high alert.
  • Mount Ili Lewotolok erupted again with an ash column reaching 700-800 meters, adding to Indonesia's concurrent volcanic activity.
  • President Prabowo wants every Indonesian to have a bank account, with BRI and BSI tasked to prepare for mass account opening.
  • The government confirmed funds are available to cover high-speed rail debt obligations.
  • President Prabowo ordered more aircraft and drones deployed to fight forest fires, and directed police to act against corporations behind land fires while ordering a comprehensive disaster mitigation master plan.
